## The finite-volume update and the flux divergence {#sec-ch04-divergence}

### Summary

Every scheme of this chapter ends in one operator. A stage of the time integrator turns the cell averages into
face fluxes, and this operator turns the face fluxes back into a change of each cell average: it adds up what
flows in and out through the faces of a cell and divides by the cell's volume. Because every face value is
added to one cell and subtracted from its neighbour, nothing is created or lost between cells, on any grid.
The operator is always on; a direction can only be switched off as a whole.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Forms $\Delta\mathbf U_i = -\Delta t\,\Delta_i[A\mathbf F]/V_i$ summed over three directions, @eq-ch04-divergence-fv.

**Data.** Reads $\mathbf F_1, \mathbf F_2, \mathbf F_3$ on faces, $A$ and $V$; writes `_div`, then $\Delta\mathbf U$ on interior cells.

**Placement.** Every RK[^rg-8e6b68aec2c7] stage, in `HydroImpl::forward`, after all face fluxes are final.

**Activation.** Always on; `dynamics/disable-flux-x1|x2|x3` drops a direction and its gravity (default false).

**Guarantee / limits.** Conservative on every grid; bitwise zero for a uniform flux on Cartesian only.

**Evidence.** @tbl-ch04-divergence-tests; `derivation_check.py` `[C1]`, `operator_check.py` `[C1]`–`[C4]`.
:::

Local symbols: $\mathbf F_a$[^rg-ba48791f181f] the numerical flux through faces normal to $x_a$ (appendix A, notation group 4); $A_{a,f}$ the area of face $f$ normal to $x_a$ [m$^2$]; $\mathcal Q$ a set of cells and $\partial\mathcal Q$
its outer faces; $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}=2^{-52}$ machine epsilon (appendix A, notation group 7), so one rounding errs by at most $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}/2$.

### Derivation

#### From the conservation law to the cell update

1. *The law.* snapy advances $\partial_t\mathbf U + \nabla\cdot\mathbf F = \mathbf S$ for the conserved vector
   $\mathbf U$[^rg-cf280b68848a] of appendix A, notation group 2. The source $\mathbf S$ belongs to other chapters; this section is the flux term.
2. *Integrate over cell $i$[^rg-b2e4785cc8b1].* The cell does not move, so the time derivative passes through the integral, and the
   divergence theorem turns the volume integral of $\nabla\cdot\mathbf F$ into the outward flux through the cell's
   faces:

   $$
   \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\int_{V_i}\mathbf U\,\mathrm{d}V
    = -\oint_{\partial V_i}\mathbf F\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}\,\mathrm{d}A .
   $$ {#eq-ch04-divergence-exact}

3. *Split the boundary into faces.* A hexahedral cell has two faces per direction. Writing the face integral in
   direction $a$ as the face area times the face average of the normal flux, $\int_f\mathbf F\cdot\hat{\mathbf n}\,
   \mathrm{d}A = A_{a,f}\langle\mathbf F_a\rangle_f$, is exact; it is a definition of the face average.
4. *Divide by $V_i$[^rg-7787d026c01f].* The left side becomes $\mathrm{d}\langle\mathbf U\rangle_{V_i}/\mathrm{d}t$, the rate of the
   stored cell average.
5. *The one approximation.* The scheme replaces each face average $\langle\mathbf F_a\rangle_f$ by the single
   number the Riemann solver returns for that face. Everything that decides the accuracy of that number lives
   in the reconstruction and the solver (@sec-ch04-framework, @sec-ch04-riemann) and in the two face-average
   corrections of section 4B.
6. *Multiply by the stage step.* One stage takes the right side times $\Delta t$[^rg-0fb11326ca3f]:

$$
\Delta\mathbf U_i = -\Delta t\sum_{a=1}^{3}\frac{A_{a,i+1/2}\mathbf F_{a,i+1/2} - A_{a,i-1/2}\mathbf F_{a,i-1/2}}{V_i},
$$ {#eq-ch04-divergence-fv}

with $i\pm\tfrac12$[^rg-5df4aa41a896] the two faces of direction $a$. `derivation_check.py` `[C1]` checks step 2 in one dimension,
$\int_{x_-}^{x_+}\partial_xF\,\mathrm{d}x = F(x_+) - F(x_-)$, with sympy. In the code, @eq-ch04-divergence-fv is `divergence` times `-dt` ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::divergence >}}).

#### Why the update conserves, on any grid

1. *Each interior face appears twice.* Face $f$ between cells $i$ and $i+1$ enters $V_i\Delta\mathbf U_i$ with
   $-\Delta t A_f\mathbf F_f$ and $V_{i+1}\Delta\mathbf U_{i+1}$ with $+\Delta t A_f\mathbf F_f$.
2. *The same number both times.* The divergence forms the face product twice, once as the upper face of cell $i$
   and once as the lower face of cell $i+1$: `face_area1` slices one element-wise formula on the same grid tensors
   ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.hpp CoordinateImpl::face_area1 >}}) and both flux slices read the one element
   `flux1[f]` ({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::divergence >}}). IEEE multiplication is correctly
   rounded, so identical operands give identical products, and the two terms are the same floating-point number
   with opposite signs.
3. *Sum over any set of cells.* For a set $\mathcal Q$ the sum $\sum_{i\in\mathcal Q}V_i\Delta\mathbf U_i$
   telescopes: only the faces of $\partial\mathcal Q$ survive. `derivation_check.py` `[C1]` sums six cells
   symbolically and gets $A_6\mathbf F_6 - A_0\mathbf F_0$, the two outer faces of the six cells; `operator_check.py` `[C4]` does it for random fluxes on a block.
4. *No geometric assumption.* Steps 1 to 3 never used the shape of the cell, so the update conserves on the
   Cartesian, spherical-polar and cubed-sphere grids alike. What breaks it is a face that carries two numbers,
   one per side; @sec-ch04-seam is the one place the code has to arrange the single value by hand.

#### Why a uniform flux gives an exact zero on Cartesian, and how large the residual is elsewhere

1. *Cartesian.* The two faces of a direction have the same area, so a flux that is the same on both gives
   $A\mathbf F - A\mathbf F$, and the difference of two identical floating-point numbers is exactly zero.
   `operator_check.py` `[C1]` finds $0$ over a $5\times4\times3$ block.
2. *Curved grids.* The areas differ, $A_{i+1/2}\ne A_{i-1/2}$, so a uniform flux leaves the geometric term
   $\mathbf F(A_{i+1/2}-A_{i-1/2})/V_i$, which the coordinate's own source cancels (@sec-ch04-sphsrc).
3. *The residual is round-off, bounded.* Write the $x_1$ term as $(a-b)/V$ with $a = A_{i+1/2}F_{i+1/2}$ and
   $b = A_{i-1/2}F_{i-1/2}$. Every floating-point operation returns its exact result times $(1+\eta)$ with
   $\lvert\eta\rvert\le\epsilon_{\mathrm m}/2$, $\epsilon_{\mathrm m} = 2^{-52}$. Count the roundings along the longest path: two in the
   area as the coordinate computes it, one in the product $AF$, one in the difference, two in the volume and one in
   the quotient, so $k = 2+1+1+2+1 = 7$. To first order in $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$[^rg-e68ce82306ee] the computed term differs from the exact one
   by at most $k\,(\epsilon_{\mathrm m}/2)(\lvert a\rvert+\lvert b\rvert)/V$.
4. *The bound for the check's field.* For $\mathbf F = r\hat r$ per unit solid angle, $a = r_+^3$, $b = r_-^3$
   and $V = (r_+^3 - r_-^3)/3$, so the bound is $3k\,(\epsilon_{\mathrm m}/2)(r_+^3 + r_-^3)/(r_+^3 - r_-^3)
   \approx k\,\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\,r/h$ for a thin cell. On the $r\in[2,3]$, $h = 1/6$ grid of
   `operator_check.py` `[C2]` its largest value, in the outermost cell, is $2.73\times10^{-14}$
   (`derivation_check.py` `[C18]`). The
   tangential fluxes of $r\hat r$ are zero, so the $x_2$ and $x_3$ terms add nothing, and the measured
   $\max\lvert\nabla\cdot(r\hat r) - 3\rvert = 3.6\times10^{-15}$ is inside the bound. The bound grows as
   $r/h$: a thin shell far from the centre loses the most digits.

**Where it runs.** `HydroImpl::forward` builds the three face fluxes, applies the seam average
(@sec-ch04-seam) and the species limiter (@sec-ch08-theta), and then calls the coordinate's `forward`, which
is `divergence` plus that grid's geometric source. The stage increment is $-\Delta t$ times the result on
interior cells only; ghost cells keep a zero increment.

**Index ranges.** Cells of direction $x_1$ run from `il()` to `iu()`, and the faces from `il()` to `iu()+1`:
`face_area1(si + 1, ei + 1) * flux1.slice(DIM1, si + 1, ei + 1)` is the upper face of every interior cell and
`face_area1(si, ei) * flux1.slice(DIM1, si, ei)` the lower one. The same slicing holds for $x_2$ and $x_3$.

**Order.** The update itself is exact (steps 1 to 4 above); the order of the scheme is the order of the face
value, set by the reconstruction (@sec-ch04-framework) and limited to second order by the face-average
approximation of step 5, and by the conversion of the cell averages to primitives (@sec-ch04-conv4), unless the
corrections of section 4B are on.

### Code

**A minimal input.** The operator has no switch of its own; three keys drop a direction's flux:

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `dynamics`[^rg-ac6e4d54428b], `disable-flux-x1`[^rg-f69e6424a96a], `disable-flux-x2`[^rg-05a4d6917e1a], `disable-flux-x3`[^rg-907281e50fb9].
```yaml
dynamics:
  disable-flux-x1: false   # default false; true keeps no x1 flux in the update
  disable-flux-x2: false
  disable-flux-x3: false
```

**What the parser accepts and refuses.** `HydroOptionsImpl::from_yaml`
({{< code src/hydro/hydro_options.cpp HydroOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}) applies, in order:

1. *`dynamics` must be a map or empty*, else "dynamics must be a map": the keys below are read by name.
2. *Unknown keys are refused* by `check_keys`; the accepted set is `equation-of-state`[^rg-30f2982a8798], `reconstruct`[^rg-cc724bd015e6],
   `riemann-solver`[^rg-1b6aaa4be991], `verbose`, `disable-flux-x1|x2|x3`, `wb-wall-clamp`[^rg-350c0bc7486d] and
   `conversion-order`[^rg-d9b0d519e18a] (@sec-ch04-conv4). A misspelt `disable-flux` key is an
   error, not a silently kept flux.
3. *A non-boolean value is refused* by the YAML[^rg-244d79da29f9] conversion of `as<bool>`.
4. *Disabling a direction also zeroes that gravity component* (`grav1(0.)` and its siblings): with no flux in
   $x_a$ there is no pressure gradient to balance $g_a$, and a kept $g_a$ would accelerate every cell without
   limit.

`divergence` itself refuses to run when no direction has a flux tensor ("At least one flux tensor must be
defined"), because the output array takes its shape from the first defined flux.

**The excerpt.** The $x_1$ part of `CoordinateImpl::divergence`
({{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::divergence >}}) and the line of `HydroImpl::forward` that
turns it into the increment ({{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}}):

```cpp
  if (flux1.defined() > 0) {
    dflx.slice(DIM1, si, ei) +=
        face_area1(si + 1, ei + 1) * flux1.slice(DIM1, si + 1, ei + 1) -
        face_area1(si, ei) * flux1.slice(DIM1, si, ei);
  }
  ...
  return dflx / vol;
  ...
  du.index(interior) = -dt * _div.index(interior);
```

The first statement is the $a = 1$ term of the sum in @eq-ch04-divergence-fv, $A_{i+1/2}\mathbf F_{i+1/2} -
A_{i-1/2}\mathbf F_{i-1/2}$; `return dflx / vol` is the division by $V_i$; the last line is the factor
$-\Delta t$ on interior cells.

| what | code link | symbol | switch |
|---|---|---|---|
| the stage operator | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `forward` | every stage |
| the increment on interior cells | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_forward.cpp HydroImpl::forward >}} | `interior` | |
| the divergence | {{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::divergence >}} | `divergence` | |
| the $x_1$ term | {{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::divergence >}} | `face_area1` | $x_1$ flux defined |
| Cartesian: divergence only | {{< code src/coord/coordinate.cpp CoordinateImpl::forward >}} | `forward` | cartesian |
| per-direction switch | {{< code src/hydro/hydro_options.cpp HydroOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}} | `disable_flux_x1` | YAML, default false |

and `[C4]` gives a telescoping residual of $1.9\times10^{-16}$ relative. The two ctest entries pass at the pin on
CPU, one rank (@tbl-ch04-ctest-run in @sec-ch04-fluxcov).

### Limits

1. **Cylindrical coordinates are not built.** The source file carries a trailing underscore and is not compiled
   (@sec-ch03).
2. **Ghost tendencies.** No increment is formed on a ghost cell, so a correction that writes one cannot reach the
   state. That is a property of the index ranges above, not an assertion in the code.
3. **One value per face.** The operator conserves only if each face carries one number. Across a process seam
   that is arranged by averaging (@sec-ch04-seam), which hides a disagreement between the two sides rather than
   removing it.
